newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary March grains futures down, others steady.
newsitem.headline: Hungary March grains futures down, others steady.

text.p: Most grains futures on the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) finished little changed on Friday after increasing in the first half of the week, traders said.
Friday's only substantial price movements were in March contracts maturing Friday as the 400 forints maximum daily limit is not in effect on the last day of any maturity.
Sunflower seed for March finished at 32,000 forints per tonne, down 1,500, as one company was unwilling to deliver, one dealer said.
March milling wheat finished 930 forints lower at 25,870.
"This is because BCE wheat prices are still higher than spot market prices and producers are more willing to sell (on the futures market)," said Robert Monostori of Agrimpex.
The drop in March prices also brought down May, which finished at 24,230 forints, down 160.
New crop milling wheat prices were little changed on Friday but Monostori expected a downward movement to start next week.
"Nobody has yet been prepared to sell at considerably lower prices, but a downward trend is bound to start in the light of international price movements," Monostori said.
"The weather is good and there is no other factor at the moment influencing prices."
March maize would also have finished lower were it not for a last-minute deal that took the price up by 100 forints to close at 17,200.
July maize, which finished at 17,050 forints, down 30, was the most active, accounting for 210 contracts out of a total turnover of 648 contracts, or 253.5 million forints.
Lot size is 20,000 kg for all contracts.
